summary: Iteration 15: Rigorous E2E testing of cross-module RBAC (module_roles + Module Switcher + module dashboards). Backend: 12/12 pytest passing on /api/module-roles/* (meta, /me legacy fallback, /org-users admin-only + 403 for non-admin, grant validates module+role + rejects cross-org + requires admin, grant persistence verified via re-login /me, revoke removes role, invalid module/role → 400). Frontend: 3 CRITICAL bugs block the core feature described in the review_request. (1) AdminRoute wraps /vendor-audit/dashboard, /register-maker/dashboard, /internal-audit/dashboard, /consultancy/dashboard — so the very users the feature is designed for (employees granted a module role) are redirected to /dashboard with isAdmin===false. (2) ModuleLoginPage hard-codes login_as='admin', so NO employee can ever log in through /hrms/login (gets 403 'You are not authorized as admin'). (3) Module Switcher lives only inside ModuleShell, which is only used by the 4 new stub dashboards; the HRMS employee Layout has NO switcher, so even after granting vendor_audit to an employee, they see no path into vendor-audit from their home /dashboard. Net: backend RBAC is solid, but the frontend wiring does not honour module_roles at all — it still uses the binary legacy admin/employee gate. Grant UI + backend grant/revoke confirmed working via API; ModuleAccessPage renders users + grant dialog with proper testids.

minor.issue: No validation of module name against MODULE_ROLES — accepts any string and does $unset silently.
Returns up to 500 users unpaginated. Fine at current scale but flagged for scale.
When target user not in same org, returns 403 — but for non-existent user_id returns 404. Acceptable, just inconsistent vs revoke which returns 404 for both.

ui_bugs.issue: Routes /vendor-audit/dashboard, /register-maker, /register-maker/dashboard, /internal-audit, /internal-audit/dashboard, /consultancy, /consultancy/dashboard are wrapped in <AdminRoute> which redirects any non-admin (isAdmin = user.role==='admin') to /dashboard. This defeats the module-roles feature — an employee granted vendor_audit/auditor gets bounced away. Need a ModuleRoute gate that checks accessible_modules (from /api/module-roles/me) instead.

Hardcoded login('admin') — employees cannot log in via /hrms/login at all (gets 403 'You are not authorized as admin'). Must either add an Admin/Employee tab like AuthPage does, or call login() with a role the backend accepts for employees.

Module Switcher is implemented inside ModuleShell, but ModuleShell is only used by the 4 new stub dashboards (VendorAuditDashboard etc.). The actual HRMS Layout wrapping /dashboard does not render the switcher, so an employee granted extra module roles never sees a switcher on their home page — they have no UI entry into the other module. Either add the switcher to Layout or render ModuleShell around HRMS Dashboard.

action_items: CRITICAL: Replace <AdminRoute> wrapping module dashboards in App.js (lines 128-135) with a new <ModuleRoute moduleKey='vendor_audit'> that checks whether user has accessible_modules.includes(moduleKey) using /api/module-roles/me (or the module_roles already on user).

CRITICAL: Fix ModuleLoginPage.js line 31 — do NOT hardcode login_as='admin'. Either add an Admin/Employee toggle (like AuthPage has) or call backend without login_as so employees can authenticate. Alternatively, backend can treat missing login_as as 'auto-detect'.

CRITICAL: Surface the Module Switcher in the HRMS Layout top-bar (not only inside ModuleShell). Currently Layout.js has no <ModuleSwitcher /> at all, so employees with 2+ modules never see it on their home page. Either embed ModuleShell around the HRMS Dashboard or lift the switcher component into Layout's topbar.
Add module-name validation to DELETE /api/module-roles/users/{uid}/revoke/{module} — reject unknown modules with 400 instead of silent $unset.
Consider adding search/filter on ModuleAccessPage (50+ test users from prior iterations clutter the list).
Add aria-describedby to ModuleAccessPage grant dialog (Radix warning).
critical_code_review_comments: accessible_modules() in module_roles.py duplicates the legacy-admin fallback logic inside two separate branches (top of fn + lower 'legacy==admin' block). Simplify by computing base set once then layering legacy fallback.
module_roles.py /me intersects with org-enabled modules AFTER computing legacy admin access to all modules — correct, but could be short-circuited if org has no modules enabled.
No audit trail for grant/revoke actions — consider logging admin_user_id + target_user_id + module + role + timestamp into a collection for security review.
Frontend ModuleShell calls /api/module-roles/me on every mount — fine but could be cached in AuthContext after login, avoiding redundant calls when switching between module dashboards.
AuthContext.isAdmin is a pure legacy-role boolean; should expose hasModuleAccess(moduleKey) helper derived from /me response to unblock ModuleRoute implementation.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend RBAC endpoints (12/12 green). Three frontend bugs need main-agent fixes before retest: (1) AdminRoute -> ModuleRoute for the 4 module dashboards, (2) ModuleLoginPage hardcodes login_as='admin' (breaks employee /hrms/login), (3) Module Switcher not mounted in HRMS Layout (only lives in ModuleShell used by stub dashboards). After fixes, retest the E2E flow: admin grants vendor_audit/auditor to employee@hrms.com -> employee logs out -> employee logs in via /hrms/login -> Module Switcher visible in topbar -> click Vendor Audit -> lands on /vendor-audit/dashboard (no 403, no redirect). Also retest priya@hrms.com (no extra roles) should NOT see switcher. ModuleAccessPage grant-dialog testids confirmed: grant-access-{userId}, grant-module-select, grant-role-select, grant-submit.
rca of the issue: The module_roles backend is complete and correct; the frontend still enforces the pre-module-roles binary admin/employee gate everywhere. AdminRoute in App.js (line 77-83) only honours user.role==='admin', never reads user.module_roles or /api/module-roles/me. The 4 new module dashboards were correctly built inside ModuleShell (which fetches /me and renders the switcher), but the shell was never added to the HRMS Layout that employees actually see. Finally, ModuleLoginPage (used by /hrms/login and 4 other per-module logins) hardcodes login_as='admin' in its handleSubmit, which is why employees cannot use the module-branded login pages at all. Three-line fix plan: (a) create ModuleRoute that calls /api/module-roles/me once via AuthContext and checks accessible.includes(moduleKey); (b) replace <AdminRoute> with <ModuleRoute moduleKey=...> for lines 128-135 of App.js; (c) lift the <ModuleSwitcher> button out of ModuleShell into Layout.js topbar so it is visible on the HRMS dashboard too; (d) remove hardcoded 'admin' in ModuleLoginPage or add an Admin/Employee toggle like AuthPage.
